subject: What's wrong with these geom_text and annotate(geom = "text") approaches?

messages.author: afa289b81aad98c2
messages.subject: What's wrong with these geom_text and annotate(geom = "text") approaches?
parts:
Hello All. It's late in the semester and I'm probably not thinking
straight, but in the function below I can't get the geom_text or
annotate approaches to label my graph. If you don't mind, uncomment
them one at a time and you'll see what I mean. Thanks for any
guidance. I never seem to get geom_text right, though I thought this
should have worked. Bryan

# Grade Distribution Plot

grdDist <- function(grd, shift = 0, ...) {
cnt <- count(grd*100)
p <- ggplot(data = cnt, aes(x, freq, ymin = 0, ymax = freq))
p <- p + geom_linerange(size = 2) + ylab("count") + xlab("grade")
p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = c(64.5, 69.5, 72.5, 76.5, 79.5,
82.5, 86.5, 89.5, 93.5) + shift,
col = "red", alpha = 0.2)

# Now make a df with just the labeling info
ym <- max(cnt$freq)*1.1
z <- data.frame(grdlet = c("F", "D", "C-", "C", "C+", "B-", "B", "B
+", "A-", "A"),
x = c(62, 66, 71, 75, 77, 81, 85, 87, 91, 95) + shift, y = ym)
print(z) # looks OK

# neither of these work quite right:
# p <- p + geom_text(aes(label = grdlet, x = x, y = y), col = "red",
data = z)
# p <- p + annotate(geom = "text", label = z$grdlet, x = z$x, y = z$y,
col = "red")
print(p)

}

grd <- c(0.76, 0.83, 0.87, 0.88, 0.81, 0.87, 0.73, 0.89, 0.77, 0.81,
0.84, 0.83, 0.88, 0.83, 0.82, 0.84, 0.83, 0.86, 0.83, 0.76)

grdDist(grd)

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: What's wrong with these geom_text and annotate(geom = "text") approaches?
parts:
Hi

try this:

p <- p + geom_text(aes(label = grdlet, x = x, y = y, ymin=NULL,
ymax=NULL), col = "red", data = z)

Since the ymin and ymax is inherited from the aes in the first
ggplot() call, geom_text automatically search the `freq` variable, and
it fails as the new data does not contains such variable.

--

The University of  Tokyo, Japan.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: What's wrong with these geom_text and annotate(geom = "text") approaches?
parts:
Hi Bryan:

I always forget to use NULL (thanks for the reminder, Kohske :), but
part of the problem is that the x's and y's in the two data frames
used have different names. The error I got when running your code in
the console was
> p + geom_text(aes(label = grdlet, x = x, y = y), col = "red", data = z)

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'freq' not found

where freq is defined as the y variable in the ggplot() call.

So I did a little rearranging :) If I know I'm going to be using two
or more data frames to render a plot, I've learned to make the initial
ggplot() call as minimal as possible and pass the aesthetics to the
geoms, where they behave locally rather than globally. This way, the x
and y used in geom_linerange() don't clash with the x and y in
geom_text() because neither x nor y is assigned globally in the
ggplot() statement.

grdDist <- function(grd, shift = 0, ...) {
cnt <- count(grd*100)

p <- ggplot(data = cnt) +
geom_linerange(aes(x = x, y = freq, ymin = 0, ymax =
freq), size = 2) +
ylab("count") + xlab("grade") +

# Now make a df with just the labeling info
ym <- max(cnt$freq)*1.1
z <- data.frame(grdlet = c("F", "D", "C-", "C", "C+", "B-",
"B", "B+", "A-", "A"),
p <- p + geom_text(aes(label = grdlet, x = x, y = y), col =
"red", data = z)

grdDist(grd)

You might want to play around with a couple of the x positions in the
text, but otherwise it looks OK to me.

HTH,
Dennis
